name: Memory and Casinos
description: There are n casinos lined in a row. If Memory plays at casino i , he has probability p i to win and move to the casino on the right ( i + 1 ) or exit the row (if i = n ), and a probability 1 - p i to lose and move to the casino on the left ( i - 1 ) or also exit the row (if i = 1 ). We say that Memory dominates on the interval i ... j if he completes a walk such that, He starts on casino i . He never looses in casino i . He finishes his walk by winning in casino j . Note that Memory can still walk left of the 1 -st casino and right of the casino n and that always finishes the process. Now Memory has some requests, in one of the following forms: 1 i a b : Set . 2 l r : Print the probability that Memory will dominate on the interval l ... r , i.e. compute the probability that Memory will first leave the segment l ... r after winning at casino r , if she starts in casino l . It is guaranteed that at any moment of time p is a non-decreasing sequence , i.e. p i ≤ p i + 1 for all i from 1 to n - 1 . Please help Memory by answering all his requests!
input_specification: The first line of the input contains two integers n and q ( 1 ≤ n , q ≤ 100 000 ),  — number of casinos and number of requests respectively. The next n lines each contain integers a i and b i ( 1 ≤ a i < b i ≤ 10 9 )  — is the probability p i of winning in casino i . The next q lines each contain queries of one of the types specified above ( 1 ≤ a < b ≤ 10 9 , 1 ≤ i ≤ n , 1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ n ). It's guaranteed that there will be at least one query of type 2 , i.e. the output will be non-empty. Additionally, it is guaranteed that p forms a non-decreasing sequence at all times.
output_specification: Print a real number for every request of type 2 — the probability that boy will "dominate" on that interval. Your answer will be considered correct if its absolute error does not exceed 10 - 4 . Namely: let's assume that one of your answers is a , and the corresponding answer of the jury is b . The checker program will consider your answer correct if | a - b | ≤ 10 - 4 .
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 712E — Memory and Casinos [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
